fps.label: FPS
fps.name: Frames per second
fps.what: EMA-smoothed frames per second from the render loop.
fps.why: The headline smoothness number — what the eye feels as fluid or choppy.
fps.interpret: ≥50 is smooth, 30–50 dips, below 30 is visibly choppy. May read 0 at startup.

fpsP50.label: p50
fpsP50.name: Median FPS (p50)
fpsP50.what: Median frames per second across the recent window (~3s).
fpsP50.why: A typical frame, unskewed by the odd spike — steadier than the live FPS.
fpsP50.interpret: Should sit near your target rate. A low p50 means sustained slowness, not a blip.

fpsP1.label: p1-low
fpsP1.name: 1%-low FPS
fpsP1.what: The 1%-low FPS — the mean of the slowest 1% of frames in the window.
fpsP1.why: Captures the worst stutters the average hides; this is what makes motion feel janky.
fpsP1.interpret: Want it close to p50. A big p50→p1 gap means occasional hard hitches.

jank.label: jank
jank.name: Jank
jank.what: Share of frames slower than the 30fps floor (33.3ms).
jank.why: A direct count of dropped-feeling frames.
jank.interpret: 0% is clean, a few % is occasional hitching, above 15% is constant stutter.

jitter.label: jitter
jitter.name: Jitter
jitter.what: Standard deviation of frame intervals, in milliseconds.
jitter.why: Evenly-paced frames feel smooth even at a lower rate; uneven ones feel worse.
jitter.interpret: Low (≈0–4ms) is steady; above 8ms is an irregular, lurching cadence.

sceneLoopMs.label: loop
sceneLoopMs.name: Scene loop time
sceneLoopMs.what: Time the scene's per-frame render loop takes, in milliseconds.
sceneLoopMs.why: The slice of the frame budget this game's own work costs — isolates app cost from the browser's.
sceneLoopMs.interpret: Keep well under the frame budget (~16ms at 60fps). Above 12ms leaves little headroom.

actorCensus.label: actors
actorCensus.name: Actor census
actorCensus.what: Live actor count — drifting items and players on the scene.
actorCensus.why: Render cost scales with actors; pileups are a common slowdown cause.
actorCensus.interpret: Higher means more to draw. Pair with loop/FPS to see if a crowd is the bottleneck.

writeSkip.label: w/s
writeSkip.name: DOM writes / skips
writeSkip.what: Per frame: item DOM writes vs writes skipped by the off-screen cull.
writeSkip.why: Shows the soft-cull working — a skipped item costs nothing to position.
writeSkip.interpret: More skips than writes means the cull is paying off on a busy scene.

restructures.label: restr
restructures.name: DOM restructures
restructures.what: DOM node add/remove operations per second (not plain attribute writes).
restructures.why: Restructures cost far more than moving existing nodes; churn signals thrash.
restructures.interpret: Low and stable is good. A high rate means actors are recreated, not reused.

gap.label: gap
gap.name: Prediction gap
gap.what: Own-sprite prediction gap: the world-pixel distance between the server position and the rendered one.
gap.why: Measures the steering rubber-band — how far client prediction drifts from authority.
gap.interpret: Tens of px is fine; hundreds is visible snapping. Shows «—» until your sprite exists.

staleness.label: stale
staleness.name: Snapshot staleness
staleness.what: Age of the latest authoritative snapshot, in milliseconds.
staleness.why: Surfaces network/throttle stalls — stale data is what prediction has to paper over.
staleness.interpret: ~300–500ms is normal cadence; above 1s means snapshots are stalling. Shows «—» until your sprite exists.
